AE Grading Overview

Study: AA-AA-000-0000

gsm.kri Example

Snapshot Date: 2026-09-03

Set Up

This page provides a sample AE Grading Report generated using the gsm.kri package. Expand the “Setup” section below to see the code used to generate the report. Or scroll down for the standard report output.

The report is the visual companion to the two site-level grading metrics, kri0016 (High-Grade AE Proportion) and kri0017 (Low-Grade AE Proportion). It is produced by Report_AEGrading(), which is wired up as the report_aegrading workflow module.

Note on the example data. The gsm.core example data has a realistic study-wide grade distribution, but grades are assigned independently of site, so no site deviates from the study and the report has nothing to find. This page therefore redraws aetoxgr with Sim_AEGrading(), keeping the real subject/site structure and per-site AE burden while giving a few sites deliberate over- and under-grading behaviour. Every number below is illustrative; the mechanics are real.

Setup 
# Load libraries
library(gsm.core)
library(gsm.mapping)
library(gsm.kri)
library(gsm.reporting)
library(dplyr)
library(tibble)

source("util/Sim_AEGrading.R")

# --- Step 1: Map raw data (real gsm.mapping pipeline) ------------------------
core_mappings <- c(
  "AE", "COUNTRY", "DATAENT", "ENROLL", "SITE", "STUDY", "SUBJ"
)

mappings_wf <- MakeWorkflowList(
  strNames = core_mappings,
  strPath = "workflow/1_mappings",
  strPackage = "gsm.mapping"
)

## This warning is displayed once per session.
## Call `lifecycle::last_lifecycle_warnings()` to see where this warning was
## generated.
lRaw <- Ingest(gsm.core::lSource, CombineSpecs(mappings_wf))

# --- Step 2: Simulate site-level grading behaviour (example only) ------------
sim <- Sim_AEGrading(lMapped$Mapped_AE, lMapped$Mapped_SUBJ)
lMapped$Mapped_AE <- sim$AE

# --- Step 3: Run the AE grading metrics --------------------------------------
metric_names <- c("kri0016", "kri0017")
metrics_wf <- MakeWorkflowList(
  strNames = metric_names,
  strPath = "workflow/2_metrics",
  strPackage = "gsm.kri"
)
lAnalyzed <- RunWorkflows(metrics_wf, c(lMapped, list(lWorkflows = metrics_wf)))

EXPERIMENTAL — FOR EXPLORATORY USE ONLY
All findings should be independently confirmed.

AE Grading Overview

This report examines how consistently investigator sites apply CTCAE severity grading to adverse events. It is a companion to the site-level grading KRIs kri0016 (High-Grade AE Proportion) and kri0017 (Low-Grade AE Proportion), and asks a single question: does a site’s distribution of Grade 1–5 events look like the rest of the study? Sites that grade nearly everything as Grade 1, or nearly everything as Grade 3/4, stand out against their peers.

6573 graded adverse events across 97 sites met the minimum volume threshold of 20 graded AEs per site. Study-wide, 24.4% of adverse events are Grade 3 or higher.

Study-wide grade distribution

Grade Events % of all AEs
Grade 1 3164 48.1%
Grade 2 1808 27.5%
Grade 3 916 13.9%
Grade 4 471 7.2%
Grade 5 213 3.2%

Grade distribution by site

Each bar is one site’s severity mix, sorted by the proportion of Grade 3+ events. Sites at the top report the highest share of severe events; sites at the bottom report the lowest. The dashed line marks the study-wide Grade 3+ proportion — bars that break well away from it in either direction are the sites whose grading behaviour differs from their peers.

Flagged sites

Site Numerator Total AEs Site % Study % Z-score Direction
0X2532 85 105 81.0% 24.4% 6.26 Over-grading
0X3289 50 69 72.5% 24.4% 4.32 Over-grading
0X4750 41 54 75.9% 24.4% 4.09 Over-grading
0X8788 2 117 1.7% 24.4% -2.65 Under-grading
0X5895 4 114 3.5% 24.4% -2.40 Under-grading
0X3909 5 99 5.1% 24.4% -2.07 Under-grading
Sites flagged by the grading metric on a two-sided adjusted z-score. Over-grading means the site reports a higher proportion of the graded events of interest than the study; under-grading, a lower proportion.

Method notes and limitations

  • Grades are treated as reported. No re-derivation from lab values or outcome data is attempted; the report measures internal consistency across sites, not clinical correctness.
  • The study is its own comparator. If grading drifts study-wide, this report will not detect it — every site is compared to the study average.
  • The overall severity mix is a blunt instrument. A site can report a perfectly average proportion of severe events while still grading individual event types inconsistently. Detecting that requires comparing sites against the study term by term, which is not part of this report.
  • Small sites are excluded. Sites below 20 graded AEs are dropped from the chart, so a small site with a genuine grading problem may not appear at all.
